shows.title: Constant Coverage #2
shows.description: Go on and tidy up - company’s here, and they’ve brought all your favorites! BIzarro Italian Bowie, swingin’ German Supremes, G-rated GG Allin! The Beastie Boys make a bad Billy Joel song worse! And the computers finally take over, but they’re starting with a mid-tier Stones song? It’s all this and more, from the party crashers at Axaxaxas Mlö, Inc.!

shows.title: An Evening of Stand-up Cosmogyny Hour#5
shows.description:
This world has been created and destroyed many times since we last spoke. We find ourselves amidst a new cycle of growth, nursing our various nectars and concoctions around the primordial petri dish open mic night we’ve ended up sticking around to see. It’s a two-drink minimum tonight, guys, and make sure to tip your mitochondria. You’ve been a great crowd.

NO TRACKLIST PROVIDED FOR THIS SHOW.

shows.description:
There’s many ways to experience a year: time is subjective and the universe is, ultimately, a deeply inefficient delivery mechanism for confusion. This week, enjoy music from and of the Karafuto Ainu, Eastern Algonquin, Kichwa Tukuru, Central Australian, and more (including the usual kaleidoscope of international punk/prog/pop/etc sounds). As of now, we’ll be starting to celebrate the confusion weekly - stay tuned!

shows.description:
The air is thick these days; we are slow, plodding ever onward (what choice do we have?) on an endless march towards shorter days. Have you examined the conduit recently? We have, and you’ll never believe what we have found: a celebration, heavy with chants, with mumbles, with screams and croons. Rejoice with us, we’ve only just begun!

shows.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Axaxaxas Mlö #24
shows.description:
It turns out it's been an entire day out here. Hour by hour, everything accumulates, until eventually the sun is back where it was and the stars are familiar once again. Or... are they? Wasn't that one a little more to the left? Wasn't that one quite a bit brighter? Whatever you call them, whatever they mean to you - the stars are all around us: a dizzying swirl of Japanese math pop, Tunisian hip hop, Polish prog, overtone, lounge, tsapiky, disco... something for everyone!

shows.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Axaxaxas Mlö #20
shows.description: As is the new custom around these+those parts (all parts of course interchangeable for easy reconfiguration), Axaxaxas Mlö closes out another tentet with a celebration. Yes, yes, they're all celebrations, but in today's world, we'll take any excuse for a party: Moroccan gnawa guitar, Pakistani Sufi flamenco guitar, the smoothest Japanese funk-rock grooves, Philly's finest Anarcho-Christian trance-punk, teenage Māori folk, and more! (Including a lengthy and dramatic appearance from the legendary no-input mixing board).

shows.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Axaxaxas Mlö #19
shows.description: Axaxaxas Mlö is awake and in a good mood. What's our secret? Egypt's hottest club music. Hyperspeed maximalist sensory-overload dance tracks. The long-overdue meeting of overtone singing and beatboxing. All sorts of experimental & traditional pop sounds from just about everywhere. And, of course, MC Hellshit + DJ Carhouse

shows.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Axaxaxas Mlö #18
shows.description: Against all some odds, Axaxaxas Mlö is still here - two weeks older but only a week & a half wiser (don't ask). It's a high-energy show this time around: dancehall, punk rock, kwaito, reggae, gqom, and more; with the usual brief detours into those dense & dreamy folky psychedelic fogs that never fully lift 'round these parts. And where will we be next time? Don't worry about it yet, we'll just be there

shows.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Axaxaxas Mlö #17
shows.description: Outside of the (imaginary) borders of (imaginary) Axaxaxas Mlö, the (all-too) real world continues. We hope that wherever you (hypothetical/aspirational) may be, this hour of sound (shaabi, candombe, jaipongan, shaabi, et al) brings you joy. In solidarity with the oppressed/embattled/imprisoned/marginalized of every nation, real and imagined (they're all imagined):

shows.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Axaxaxas Mlö #16
shows.description: We stray from the path so frequently here, in this world. But a path can only lead where others have already led, and leaders frequently disappoint. At least, as they say, all roads lead to Axaxaxas Mlö. And so do playlists, in their way. Let's follow this one, shall we? Deep Korean reggae. Mongolian shaman rock. Ancient wax cylinder flamenco fragments and the world's biggest star, all together at last. Luckily, wherever we end up, we'll meet you there again in a couple of weeks.

shows.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Axaxaxas Mlö #15
shows.description: Music is a way through. Not the only way, but it's a big one - and you can clear quite a path. So enjoy today's path, won't you: we've got Thai, Mexican, Iranian, Umoⁿhoⁿ, Sumatran (by way of Deep Maine); reggaeton, ohayashi, experimental flamenco, the chillest boogie pop and maybe a familiar tune or two. And there's more! There's always more. Seek it out and listen close.

shows.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Axaxaxas Mlö #14
shows.description: At last, it's the edition we've all been waiting for since last edition - another hourlong meandering around the vast unknown and in betweens. With appearances from a Japanese outsider jaw-harp troubadour, an electro-Nigerian Lionel Richie cover, a joyous Alabaman Sacred Harp rendition, and all of the usual punk dance psych funk pop warbles chants and shouts. Safe travels!

shows.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Axaxaxas Mlö #13
shows.description: welcome back to axaxaxas mlö, where we're carefully shoveling the last bits of 2025 into the ocean/inland sea/freshwater pond. join us for a sampling of some of our favorite music of the year: from the delightful returns of Noura Mint Seymali and Ata Kak to new discoveries Kasai, Yalla Miku and Ya Tosiba; new music from MC Yallah, Ammar 808, and Keiji Haino. plus, more! start the year off right.

shows.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Axaxaxas Mlö #12
shows.description:
In this twelfth manifestation of Axaxaxas Mlö, we celebrate the mighty Reissue with some of our favorite new-old music of the year. From the disorientingly slooooow cumbia rebajada of Sonido Dueñez to the sacred and otherworldly begena of Akalu Yossef, with stops along the way for Yat-Kha's Tuvan industrial grooves, the swinging kwaito of Johannesburg's Moskito, and an extended stay in Ghana, Benin and Zimbabwe for a flight of classic highlife & Afro-rock.


CIVILISTJÄVEL! + MAYSSA JALLAD » ALICK NKHATA » SONIDO DUEÑEZ » RUINSZU » MOSKITO » ZÉ CARLOS » YAT-KHA » AKALU YOSSEF » GNONNAS PEDRO & HIS DADJES BAND » ZIG ZAG BAND » OLIVER & THE BLACK SPIRITS » PAA JUDE » KING SOLOMON (NII MANTSE)



Enjoy the memories, and come back next week for the year's new music highlights!

shows.description: The air is thinner here. I can finally breathe with great relief, and my lungs fill with the sounds of Axaxaxas Mlö. It sounds different than I remembered, and changes with the time of day (present company excluded). When I release my breath, I hear something I've never heard before: Contemporary Scots folk. Bizarro French zeuhl-wave. Minimalist Slovakian ambience. Half-recalled murmurations. Frantic Jordanian dance beats. Reminisce with us, over songs old and new.

shows.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Axaxaxas Mlö #7
From the Mixed-Up Files of Axaxaxas Mlö #6
shows.description: In case you haven't noticed yet, Axaxaxas Mlö (as is the case with all hyperobjects), is never closer than it appears, and always further away than it seems. Enjoy with us a sampling of its many offerings: Sacred songs from Greece, India and beyond... Profane songs from Japan, Brazil, and nowhere. New wave, psychedelic mariachi, and a new take on an old favorite.

shows.title: An Evening of Stand-Up Cosmogony, Hour #1
shows.description:
the first night begins like any other - until an act of profound nepotism radiates outward amongst the cosmic microwave background murmuration. expansion, once triggered, sets in quickly, to an erratic beat. voices appear and disappear in the murk of a vast precellular sludge.
theories abound that some consciousness, still epochs away, has discovered a means of projecting intention (the strongest force in any universe tbd) backwards, downstream, to the heart of this as-yet-intentionless cosmos. it begins to spin a fiction.
